structure_reference: partner_dv_dbt / travel_dv_dbt -- models/staging/<lob>/ and models/automate_dv/{standard/{stitched,staging,hubs,links,satellites,references},augmented/{staging,satellites}}. Followed exactly.

macro_library.note: Same pins as partner_dv_dbt and travel_dv_dbt. Every hub, link and satellite is an automate_dv macro call and every hash is computed by automate_dv.stage(). No hash is written by hand.

inputs_pinned.note: Exactly the inputs the previous health build (v4) consumed, read in place from the mapper's bundle (read-only, BUILD_RULES s9). Each file's md5 is asserted before use; a moved file stops the build rather than being read.

not_read.SourceMapping_Skill/Health Consolidated/: moved upstream after v4 was built (v4 pinned md5 8ca871f2bee58df78e4dd3c9869fa551). v4 built from the JSON map, not the workbook, and so does this build.

inputs_pinned.delta3_run_label_note: the delta 3 map carries no source_run; the label is stamped on read. Neither map is rewritten.

legacy_key_source.what: The legacy half (opus_health_legacy_v4) carries no resolved_key in the map. Its business-key expressions exist only in health_dv_dbt's emitted automate_dv stage models: derived NK columns of the form 'HUB_X|' || <expr>, and the parent_bk column of each stitched view's per-table CTE. Those expressions are read, never their hashes.
precedence: (table, satellite) form from a stitch or a stg2_sat file
(table, hub) form when exactly one distinct expression exists
the map's own hub_key row for (table, hub)

central_view_rule.verbatim: 1. we create a central view from source tables (by joining them , max upto 10). The join are selected so that it can feed sat as a whole (one or moew). That is we do not split sat across these views. Restriction of 10 can be broken if a sat needs more than source tables to build. If a view as less source tables join, we add more tables to it efficiently so that new sats can be built.
central_view_rule.hub_and_link_extension_verbatim: the views will have hub keys -- effectively each sat is primary key goes to hub -- so hub has to come from there, 2nd the links will also be from same view , as different hub keys and sat populatin comes from there

source_precedence.note: Where two tables in one central view write the same attribute for the same key, the lower rank wins. v2 is the settled half, legacy next, delta 3 last. Within one run, tables are ranked by name and rows by a hash of the row, so the choice is deterministic.

conventions.hashdiff: HASHDIFF (bare, one stage per satellite, as partner/travel/health_dv_dbt)
conventions.role_satellites: satellites parented on the one-hub LNK_PARTY_ROLE are built off HUB_PARTY with a literal ROLE_TYPE_CK (the ratified M3 role-special pattern used by health_dv_dbt, partner_dv_dbt and travel_dv_dbt)
conventions.load_datetime: !CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()  -- kept exactly as travel/partner/health_dv_dbt write it, by the user's instruction
conventions.payload_names: UPPER_SNAKE of the data_7.js attribute name

staging_casts: every column nullif(trim(to_varchar("COL")), '') aliased lower-case. The pinned inputs carry no datatype catalogue for the legacy and v2 halves, so no type is inferred.
row_filters_note: table -> SQL predicate applied in that table's staging model. EMPTY on purpose: the mapper states row filters (TOP_INDICATOR='Y', DELETE_FLAG='0') only in key_derivation PROSE and calls the 'Y' polarity convention, not proof. A filter read out of prose is a guess; adding one here is a one-line data change once confirmed.
refusals_not_fallbacks: A key, child key or attribute that cannot be resolved from the pinned inputs is REFUSED and registered in build_artifacts/reports/unresolved_register.json with whose call it is. A fallback always produces a row, so it never produces an error.
